headline: 6 killed as fire destroys Cox’s Bazar resort
summary: At least six people died after a massive fire broke out at a resort in Cox's Bazar, leaving several others injured.
details: A devastating fire broke out at a resort in Cox's Bazar, resulting in the deaths of at least six people. The blaze destroyed the resort property and left several others injured.
The incident occurred at the 'Tup Tup' resort located in Inani, Cox's Bazar. Firefighters worked to bring the blaze under control while rescue operations were conducted.
According to various reports, several bodies were recovered from the site, and the injured have been transported to local hospitals for treatment.
Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire, though the exact origin of the blaze has not yet been confirmed.

headline: PM Tareq Rahman visits hospitals and schools to assess dengue, urges cleanliness
summary: The Prime Minister conducted surprise visits to healthcare facilities and educational institutions in Dhaka to monitor the dengue situation and call for public cooperation in cleanliness.
details: Prime Minister Tareq Rahman conducted surprise visits to several hospitals, educational institutions, and government buildings in Dhaka on Saturday morning to assess the dengue situation and overall cleanliness.

During a visit to the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital, the PM expressed dissatisfaction with the overall management and cleanliness of the facility, giving the authorities seven days to improve the conditions.
At Rajuk Uttara Model College, the PM spoke with students, teachers, and scouts, emphasizing that prevention is the most effective way to combat dengue, which typically peaks around November.
He urged students to take responsibility for keeping their homes, schools, and neighborhoods clean, stating that the युवा (youth) can bring about a significant change in environmental protection.
The PM noted that while city corporations work regularly, their capacity is limited, and citizens must take personal responsibility for waste management and preventing littering.
He expressed concern over the theft of dustbins and tree saplings planted by the North and South City Corporations, calling for more civic responsibility from the city's residents.
To combat rising temperatures and the lack of greenery in Dhaka, the PM suggested that students and their families plant at least one tree on every birthday and anniversary.
He shared childhood memories of a greener Dhaka and emphasized that increasing tree cover would help reduce the city's temperature and provide a few more breathable spaces.
caption:
PM Tareq Rahman gives hospital authorities 7 days to clean up after surprise visit. Prevention is the key to fighting dengue.

Prime Minister Tareq Rahman conducted surprise visits to several hospitals, educational institutions, and government buildings in Dhaka on Saturday morning to assess the dengue situation and overall cleanliness.

During a visit to the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital, the PM expressed dissatisfaction with the overall management and cleanliness of the facility, giving the authorities seven days to improve the conditions.

At Rajuk Uttara Model College, the PM spoke with students, teachers, and scouts, emphasizing that prevention is the most effective way to combat dengue, which typically peaks around November.

He urged students to take responsibility for keeping their homes, schools, and neighborhoods clean, stating that the युवा (youth) can bring about a significant change in environmental protection.

The PM noted that while city corporations work regularly, their capacity is limited, and citizens must take personal responsibility for waste management and preventing littering.

He expressed concern over the theft of dustbins and tree saplings planted by the North and South City Corporations, calling for more civic responsibility from the city's residents.

To combat rising temperatures and the lack of greenery in Dhaka, the PM suggested that students and their families plant at least one tree on every birthday and anniversary.

He shared childhood memories of a greener Dhaka and emphasized that increasing tree cover would help reduce the city's temperature and provide a few more breathable spaces.
